title: Case Studies
summary: Analyze the statistical efficiency and architectural requirements of interleaving versus standard A/B testing.

blocks.md:
This lesson follows **Case Studies** in *ML Operations at Scale* (Vol II). By the end you should be able to:

- Analyze the statistical efficiency and architectural requirements of interleaving versus standard A/B testing
- Explain the historical engineering drivers behind early enterprise feature store platforms
- Analyze the architectural split between offline precomputation and real-time streaming in low-latency recommendation platforms
- Identify the deployment terminology for non-serving live traffic evaluation

blocks.source: Vol II, ML Operations at Scale, § Case Studies
blocks.md: When hundreds of engineers train and deploy thousands of models against shared data streams and strict latency budgets, bespoke per-team pipelines collapse under silent feature skew, duplicated glue code, and uncoordinated rollouts. The five platform cases that follow instantiate the operations trade-offs developed earlier in this chapter: standardization vs. team-local velocity, abstraction vs. control, freshness vs. cost, and governance vs. autonomy. Each case shows a different way to keep a multi-model fleet repeatable without turning every model into bespoke infrastructure.

blocks.title: Map of the section
blocks.md:
The section is organised as:

- Uber Michelangelo
- Meta FBLearner Flow
- Netflix ML infrastructure
- Google Vertex AI
- Spotify ML platform
- Comparing platform control planes

Pay attention to: Netflix Interleaving vs. A/B testing efficiency; Uber Michelangelo and repeatable shared workflows; Spotify case: batch and online freshness trade-offs.

blocks.prompt: Think first: What general batch-versus-online design trade-off does the Spotify case illustrate for personalization features with different freshness requirements?
blocks.md: Freshness-tolerant work can be precomputed in batch, while recent-context features need an online or streaming path. Shared definitions and lineage must preserve consistency across those paths. This is the case's general design lesson, not evidence for a particular Spotify embedding, similarity-matrix, or weekend-job implementation.

questions.q: Netflix reported ranking experiments requiring over \$100× fewer users than traditional between-subject A/B tests. Which mechanism explains why interleaving can provide this sample-efficiency advantage?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Interleaving mixes two ranked lists for the same user and attributes engagement to the source ranker. Within-user comparisons reduce user-level variation and can require far fewer participants; the reported 100-fold gain applies to particular experiments, not every ranking comparison. Synthetic bots or relaxed significance thresholds do not supply the same evidence.
questions.hint: Think about: analyze the statistical efficiency and architectural requirements of interleaving versus standard A/B testing.
options: By testing ranking algorithms exclusively on synthetic bot agents.
By deploying 'Interleaving', which blends ranked lists from two algorithms into a single presentation for each user, removing user-level variance and measuring direct head-to-head clicks.
By relaxing statistical power thresholds from $\beta = 0.80$ to $\beta = 0.10$.
By evaluating models purely on historical offline training set accuracy.

questions.q: What recurring coordination problem does the Michelangelo case illustrate?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Shared feature and workflow contracts make model development repeatable across product teams. The case describes varied tools and custom production systems, rather than establishing a specific Python-to-C++/Java rewrite requirement. Standardizing delivery does not remove each team's responsibility for model behavior.
questions.hint: Think about: explain the historical engineering drivers behind early enterprise feature store platforms.
options: Cloud GPU instances were unsupported by Uber's container runtimes.
Data scientists were legally prohibited from executing SQL queries against production databases.
Varied modeling tools and custom production systems lacked a common deployment path and reproducible data pipelines.
Mobile device operating systems refused to display recommendation rankings with more than five items.

questions.q: The deployment practice where a candidate model receives copied live traffic to evaluate latency, memory, and outputs without serving its predictions to users is known as shadow deployment or ____.
questions.explanation: dark launching. Candidate outputs are not served, but resource contention and side effects still require isolation. Shadow evidence supports operational comparison rather than proving user-outcome gains.
questions.hint: Think about: identify the deployment terminology for non-serving live traffic evaluation.

points: You can now analyze the statistical efficiency and architectural requirements of interleaving versus standard A/B testing.
You can now explain the historical engineering drivers behind early enterprise feature store platforms.
You can now analyze the architectural split between offline precomputation and real-time streaming in low-latency recommendation platforms.
You can now identify the deployment terminology for non-serving live traffic evaluation.
